assertions.name: slope_10A5_refuted_at_A_ge_5
assertions.source: THE FINDING: |dev| > 5 for all of 6Li, 7Li, 7Be (measured 22.7, 30.8, 32.6) -- the slope collapses from ~10/nucleon to ~1, refuting the global A-law. Scope-(a): the global reading is excluded, the crossing bookkeeping is not.

assertions.name: slope_10A5_holds_at_A_le_4_within_0p5
assertions.source: EXPECTED RED. |dev| for D, T, 4He measures 0.63, 1.02, 1.70 -- none below the 0.5 bar this claim asserts. The <0.5 figure came from a docstring table (-0.01/-0.07/+0.27) that was stale in every row. Whether 0.5 was ever the right bar is left open: light_bar_needed reports the smallest threshold the data would satisfy.

assertions.name: proton_excess_penalty_sign_negative_both_pairs
assertions.source: proton-rich member below mirror at A=3 AND A=7 (sign derived from proton intra-writhe 3 > neutron 1)

description: Slope test + Z-coefficient test on the canonical residual Δ_λ. (1) SLOPE: log_q0 Δ_λ ≈ 10A−5 holds ONLY for A≤4 (slope ~10); at A≥5 (⁶Li/⁷Li/⁷Be) it collapses to ~0.4–2.7/nucleon — the global 10A−5 extrapolation is REFUTED (scope-(a)): B_pred saturates while B_AME grows linearly, so log Δ_λ grows logarithmically; slope-10 was a light-nucleus coincidence broken at the ⁴He shell. (2) Z-CORRECTION: the proton-excess penalty (mirror-pair split) is −1.33 at A=3 (³He/T) and −1.77 at A=7 (⁷Be/⁷Li) — SIGN derived from the p≠n intra-writhe seed (proton +3 > neutron +1), MAGNITUDE O(−1.5) but not a single derivable constant (no fit; Δ_λ gate). NOT wired.

slope_test.verdict: 10A−5 is a light-nucleus (A≤4) artifact; the global A-law is refuted at A≥5 (scope-limited negative (a)).
slope_test.root_cause: B_pred saturates (~0.7-0.8); B_AME ~linear ⇒ log Δ_λ ~logarithmic ⇒ slope-10 unsustainable past ⁴He shell

z_correction.magnitude: O(−1.5)/excess-proton; −1.33 (A=3) vs −1.77 (A=7), ~33% drift ⇒ NOT a single derivable constant (no fit)
z_correction.interpretation: bar-odd Z-correction survives the bar-even leading collapse — independent channels, as the writhe split predicts
